definitions.explanation: The arrangement of troops, players, or personnel in strategic positions. Originally a military term, now commonly used in sports, business, and politics to describe how people or resources are positioned.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{布陣|ふじん}で{臨|のぞ}む。
examples.english: To go in with a new lineup.

examples.japanese: {監督|かんとく}は{守備|しゅび}{重視|じゅうし}の{布陣|ふじん}を{敷|し}いた。
examples.english: The manager set up a defense-focused formation.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}は{新|しん}プロジェクトに{向|む}けて{精鋭|せいえい}を{集|あつ}めた{布陣|ふじん}を{整|ととの}えた。
examples.english: The president assembled an elite lineup for the new project.

notes: Common collocations: {布陣|ふじん}を{敷|し}く (to set up a formation), {布陣|ふじん}を{整|ととの}える (to arrange a lineup), {新|あたら}しい{布陣|ふじん} (a new formation/lineup). Frequently used in sports commentary, especially soccer ({4|よん}-{4|よん}-{2|に}の{布陣|ふじん}, a 4-4-2 formation) and in business/political reporting about personnel arrangements. A homophone of {夫人|ふじん} (wife) and {婦人|ふじん} (woman), but distinct in meaning and kanji.
